rounds.text: NPR Finance Ltd trades at an exorbitant price-to-earnings ratio of 61.4x, which is vastly higher than the sector benchmark of 20.12x [E1, E6]. This massive valuation premium is completely disconnected from the company's deteriorating fundamentals, highlighted by a severe trailing twelve-month profit contraction of -64% and a 10-year compounded profit growth of -6% [E18, E21]. Operational momentum is also fading rapidly, demonstrated by a sharp year-over-year sales decline of -49% alongside poor 5-year sales growth of -2.70% [E61, E67]. Furthermore, expectations have dangerously detached from reality as recent price growth exceeds profit growth by 44%, while the company fails to return any capital to shareholders with a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E55]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio sits at an optically low 0.26x against a sector benchmark of 1.36x, and 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growths show positive rates of 17% and 28% respectively [E2, E7, E19, E20].

Conceded: the trailing twelve-month profit contracted by -64% [E21] and sales fell -49% year-over-year [E67]. However, the bear relies too heavily on short-term noise while ignoring the strong medium-term earnings expansion, which shows 3-year compounded profit growth at 28% and 5-year growth at 17% [E19, E20]. The excessive focus on the 61.4x P/E ratio [E1] completely misinterprets the asset-backed reality of the business, which trades at a steep discount with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.26x compared to the sector benchmark of 1.36x [E2, E7]. This creates a massive margin of safety where the market capitalisation sits at a mere ₹ 12.9 Cr [E3] while resting near the bottom of its range at only 16% of the 52-week spread [E5]. Finally, the screen explicitly catches accelerating earnings growth as a core positive catalyst [E65], proving that the structural turnaround is already underway despite recent headline volatility.
